# V2 Stage 5 — the formal 8-method comparison, the ablation ladder and seed-clustered statistics

*Generated by `reproduce_stage5.py` from the Stage-5 CSVs; do not edit by hand.  Shipped configuration `config_id = 89fe865b2e1d` (Stage-3 frozen tuple `T_PRE / T_DIVERT / T_REC / h = 12 / 8 / 15 / 3 s`, animal 25 m, obstacle 70 m, M1, 36:12, W = 8 m).  Python 3.13.7, numpy 2.5.2, scipy 1.17.1, `jobs = 12`, BLAS pinned to one thread.*

---

## 0. Executive summary

**The one-sentence result.**  Among the methods that both keep the flock on the path (ρ ≥ 0.99) and finish every run (arrival = 1.00) — `Ours_rollout`, B1 and B2 — the shipped method has the lowest contact fraction (0.008, vs 0.108 for B1 and 0.079 for B2) and is the only one whose worst-case animal–obstacle surface clearance is positive (0.64 m vs -0.91 and -0.57 m).  Every other baseline reaches a comparable contact fraction only by leaving the task: B-Outmost ρ = 0.52 (joint completion 0.08), B-PCBF ρ = 0.44 and arrival 0.08, the VH family ρ = 0.88–0.93 with joint completion 0.39–0.42.

1. **Safety, with the denominator stated.**  C = 0.008 (rank 2 of 8; the only lower value is B-PCBF's 0.005, from a method that abandons 275/300 runs).  Worst-case clearance 0.64 m, min TTC 0.94 s.  The seed-clustered family (§7) makes all four C / clearance contrasts against B1 and B2 significant after Holm, and 38 of 49 tests in the family are significant at α = 0.05.
2. **Completion is not sacrificed.**  Arrival is 1.000 (300/300) and joint completion 0.787, against 0.803 for B1 — the difference is not significant (exact McNemar, §7.3).  The contact reduction is therefore not bought with task failure on the 36:12 family.
3. **The rollout is the mechanism, not the event layer.**  On V2S2R2 the four-state, handover and event rungs are **bit-identical** (C = 0.017 for all three, 60/60 cell pairs), and on V2S3 they differ only marginally (C = 0.350 / 0.337 / 0.341); adding the planner takes C to 0.003 and 0.017 respectively and adds +0.67 m / +1.51 m of clearance (§6).  The Stage-4 pilot's screening statement survives, now with n = 30.
4. **Preemption is real and was mis-measured.**  25 of the 30 V2S3 seeds show a genuine information-set preemption (always by threat 2, the designed case), 0 under the truth reading and 0 under the frozen legacy column (§1.1).
5. **Two families, and where they disagree.**  38/49 significant in the seed-clustered family vs 43/49 in the run-level family; 9 pairs disagree at α = 0.05 and 2 show a genuine sign reversal of the median difference (§7.4).
6. **Censoring and cost.**  377/2400 runs are censored (B-PCBF alone 275/300), all kept in the denominators; the matrix took 3.00 h at `jobs = 12` (§9).

**What this does *not* say.**  It does not say the method is safest in absolute terms (robot–animal contact is negative for every method that herds, `clr_rs` in §8); it does not say it is the best task-completer (B1 is 0.016 higher and the difference is not significant); and it does not extend to the 60:20 scene, where the method's clearance is negative and joint completion is 0.10 (§10.1 item 3).

## 1. The three blocking fixes, before any Stage-5 number was produced

### 1.1 Item 1 — `preempt_ok` measured the wrong quantity

`metrics.summarize` (frozen V1 code, untouched) derives `preempt_ok` from the log's `ttc_each`, which `sim_v2` builds from the **truth** positions of every obstacle whether or not the controller has detected it.  On V2S3/seed 1000 the truth onset of obstacle 2 is 68.5 s while the first RECOVER window opens at 69.7 s, so the frozen column says *False* although the observable threat (detected 70.2 s, TTC 9.71 s) arrives inside the window and truncates it.

Stage 5 therefore reports **two** readings and never mixes them:

* `preempt_ctrl` — **the paper's statistic**.  A threat whose *gated* risk onset (first control tick at which it is in the published view and its TTC ≤ T_PRE) falls inside an existing RECOVER window `(a, b]` and was not already in risk at `a`.  The gated TTC is recorded **inside the run at the publish instant** (`v2/stage5/probe.py`), i.e. it is literally the information the controller had.
* `preempt_truth` — the truth-based variant, from the frozen truth series.
* `preempt_legacy` — the old `metrics.preempt_ok`, kept in the CSVs for provenance only, and **not** a preemption statistic.
The measurement needed one extra fact, which changed the implementation: masking the *logged* truth series by visibility would have been wrong, because `sim_v2` writes the log row one integration step **after** the control instant.  The probe measures the size of that error on real cells:

<!-- REPRO:gated -->
| cell | ticks | pairs | max \|pub − truth\| pos [m] | max \|TTC_pub − TTC_truth\| [s] | max \|TTC_logged − TTC_truth\| (near band) [s] | onset shift [s] | preempt ctrl / truth(log) / truth(instant) / legacy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| V2S3/Ours_rollout/1000 | 2110 | 690 | 0.00e+00 | 0.00e+00 | 5.83 | 0.40 | 1 / 0 / 0 / 0 |
| V2S2/Ours_rollout/2000 | 1286 | 218 | 0.00e+00 | 0.00e+00 | 3.11 | 0.30 | 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 |
| V2S2/B1/2000 | 1296 | 218 | 0.00e+00 | 0.00e+00 | 1.43 | 0.30 | 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 |
| V2S1/Ours_rollout/2000 | 1293 | 0 | 0.00e+00 | 0.00e+00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | -1 / -1 / 0 / 0 |

Column 5 (`|TTC_pub − TTC_truth|` at the same instant) is 0.0 — the published track *is* the truth obstacle (position and velocity bit-identical) and the animal channel carries all 36 animals, so the probe's TTC is exactly the controller's.  Column 6 shows that the logged series is a *different* quantity: even inside the risk band it deviates by seconds (the analytic TTC is almost flat near tangency, so a 0.05 s state offset is not a 0.05 s TTC offset), and far from the band by tens of seconds.  Onsets read from it shift by ≤ 0.4 s — enough to matter for a 1.0 s window, and exactly why the paper's column is the publish-instant one.  The last column confirms that the truth-side flag is nevertheless stable across the two time bases (log vs instant) on every probe cell, which is what makes `preempt_truth` usable as a sensitivity variant.

**The Stage-4 D case re-verified.**  Re-running V2S3/Ours_rollout/seed 1000 reproduces the stored transcript exactly (C = 0.0278 = 1/36, min_dist = 1.4352 m, 2110 control ticks, RECOVER windows 69.70–70.70, 82.70–92.20, 149.20–151.20 s) and now reports `preempt_ctrl = 1`, `preempt_truth = 0`, `preempt_legacy = 0`.  The defect is fixed; the truth-based readings stay False exactly as Stage 4 documented.

Preemption over the formal matrix:

<!-- REPRO:preempt -->
| method | runs with RECOVER | windows | closed | preempted | open at end | preempt_ctrl = True | preempt_truth = True | legacy = True |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ours_rollout | 240 | 297 | 271 | 25 | 0 | 25 | 0 | 0 |
| B1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| B2 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| VH-Path | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| VH-Danger | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| VH-Danger-path | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| B-Outmost | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| B-PCBF | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

Preemption is only *defined* for a method that has a RECOVER state; the baselines have none, so their zeros are structural.  `preempt_ctrl` is the paper's reading (controller information set), `preempt_truth` the truth-based sensitivity variant, `legacy` the frozen `metrics.preempt_ok` column (kept for provenance only — it is **not** a preemption statistic).

Read the denominators, not the zeros: a baseline without a four-state machine has no RECOVER window, so preemption is *undefined* for it (not false).  Only `Ours_rollout` produces RECOVER windows in the formal matrix, and it is the only method for which the column carries information.

### 1.2 Item 2 — `T_REC = 15 s` re-validated at 220 m

Rule R3 of the Stage-3 calibration is `T_REC = T_PRE + max(h, ceil_0.5(median RECOVER duration))`, derived from seven V1 episodes whose median was 1.10 s.  Stage 4's three-window sample (1.0 / 9.5 / 2.0 s, one of them preempted) left the median ambiguous, so the rule has to be re-derived on the episodes that actually **closed**.  The sweep (3 values × 2 scenes × 5 calibration seeds 1000–1004, never the evaluation seeds):

| scene | T_REC [s] | windows | closed | preempted | open at end | median closed dur [s] | max closed dur [s] | median re-entry delay [s] | C | min clr_so [m] | ρ | arrival | goal time [s] |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| V2S3 | 12.5 | 15 | 10 | 5 | 0 | 3.00 | 9.50 | 3.00 | 0.0389 | -0.13 | 0.999 | 1.00 | 208.7 |
| V2S3 | 15.0 | 15 | 10 | 5 | 0 | 3.00 | 9.50 | 3.00 | 0.0389 | -0.13 | 0.999 | 1.00 | 208.7 |
| V2S3 | 18.0 | 15 | 10 | 5 | 0 | 3.00 | 9.50 | 3.00 | 0.0389 | -0.13 | 0.999 | 1.00 | 208.7 |
| V2S2 | 12.5 | 5 | 5 | 0 | 0 | 3.30 | 3.90 | 3.30 | 0.0000 | 1.04 | 0.999 | 1.00 | 126.3 |

Rule R3 on the closed windows of V2S3 at the frozen 15 s: 10 episodes, median 3.00 s → T_REC = 15.0 s.

The conclusion is in §5.4; the frozen value is **not** changed by this pass without evidence.

### 1.3 Item 3 — C1 is vacuous, and why

Stage 4 reported `C1 violations = 0` while also reporting that C1 never binds.  A bound that never engages cannot be violated, so the zero carries no information.  There are two independent reasons, and the audit establishes both:

1. **The band is degenerate for the shipped animal.** M1 uses `s_lo = m_s_min = 0` (the author decision that animals may stop), so the C1 lower bound it must respect is 0.  `limits_v2` has no C1-*upper* counter; the upper bound `s_hi = m_v_max = 2.0` is enforced through the C3 speed clip.
2. **Even the V1 band cannot bind under the frozen dynamics.**  `c1_low` fires only when the C2 turn clip admits a turn at which the reachable speed set misses `s_lo`; with `A = a_sheep·dt = 0.20 m/s` that needs `|Δθ| ≥ asin(A/s_old) ≥ 0.150 rad` (only for `s_old > 1.34`) *and* `s_lo > sqrt(s_old² − A²) ≥ 1.325`, and no admissible `s_lo ≤ 1.5` satisfies both.  The C2 cap (0.15 rad/tick) is smaller than the turn at which the bound first becomes unreachable.  The grid scan makes this concrete: with the shipped M1 band the reachable box has **0** binding cells, and with the V1 band [1.0, 1.5] it also has **0**; relaxing the C2 cap to 8 rad/s (keeping the V1 band) produces 208 binding cells, which isolates the cap as the mechanism.
<!-- REPRO:c1 -->
| configuration | a_sheep [m/s²] | ω_sheep [rad/s] | C1-low band s_lo [m/s] | binding cells |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| shipped_M1 | 4.0 | 3.0 | 0.0 | 0 |
| shipped_M0_band | 4.0 | 3.0 | 1.0 | 0 |
| turn_cap_relaxed | 4.0 | 8.0 | 1.0 | 208 |
| stress_a1_msmin1 | 1.0 | 3.0 | 1.0 | 56 |
| a2_msmin1 | 2.0 | 3.0 | 1.0 | 50 |

| runs | config | bind_C1_low (total) | violation_C1_low | C | ρ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| shipped | `89fe865b2e1d` | 0 | 0 | 0.0231 | 1.000 |
| stress | `a7253b4d6ada` | 500054 | 0 | 0.1019 | 0.959 |

Grid rows are exhaustive evaluations of the real `project_sheep_increment` over the **reachable** `(s_old, Δθ)` box — `s_old` only inside the model's own admissible band, because evaluating the projector outside it produces spurious flags that say nothing about the simulator.  `stress_a1_msmin1` and `a2_msmin1` show where the bound *does* engage, and `turn_cap_relaxed` isolates the C2 cap.  The six stress runs (`m_s_min = 1.0`, `a_sheep = 1.0`) demonstrate the machinery working: `bind_C1_low = 500 054` animal-steps with `violation_C1_low = 0`.  **In the formal matrix, however, the C1 zero-violation result is reported as carrying no information** — it is not presented as a satisfied constraint.

## 3. The eight methods and the ablation ladder

| label | what it is |
|---|---|
| `Ours_rollout` | the shipped method: four-state FSM + handover + event layer + receding-horizon rollout planner, layered speed policy |
| B1 | path shepherding only, no risk logic (`NormalHerder`) |
| B2 | distance-threshold reactive (`DistanceThreshHerder`, V1-calibrated threshold) |
| VH-Path | virtual-herder baseline, path task mode |
| VH-Danger | virtual herder, mixed danger-mode (the mechanism) |
| VH-Danger-path | the same control law in its strongest task variant |
| B-Outmost | outmost-herding baseline (T-RO 2024, mechanism-level reproduction; the authors did not release code) |
| B-PCBF | PCBF baseline (RA-L 2026, mechanism-level reproduction) |

The ladder is mechanically derived, one mechanism per rung:

| rung | class | what it adds |
|---|---|---|
| R0_four_state | `proposed.Proposed` | four-state FSM only |
| R1_handover | `proposed_improved.HandoverProposed` | + handover of the avoidance slot |
| R2_event | `proposed_event.EventProposed` | + event layer (= the pilot's `Ours_event`, i.e. **w/o rollout**) |
| R3_rollout | `proposed_rollout.RolloutProposed` through the Stage-2 `OursRolloutV2` stack | + the rollout planner (= `Ours_rollout`) |

The ladder runs on the two scenes that carry the evidence — **V2S2R2** (the V2 equivalent of S2R2) and **V2S3** — × seeds 2000–2029 = 240 runs.  R3 is built by the same factory the formal matrix uses, so its 60 rows are bit-identical to the corresponding formal `Ours_rollout` cells (checked in §4.D).

The A comparator deserves a note.  `results_v2_stage4/_smoke/detail.csv` is stamped **15:25**, i.e. *before* the 15:46 spacing freeze, and its V2S3 rows describe a superseded scene (2077 control ticks instead of 2110) — it cannot serve as a bit-exactness reference.  A1 therefore compares against `_det_j1/detail.csv` (16:22, post-freeze) and A3 against the Stage-4 D transcript.  This is the same stale-artefact trap that Stage 4 hit with the sequence trace, and the same lesson: check the artefact's timestamp before comparing to it.

### 5.4 The `T_REC` decision at 220 m

**The frozen 15 s is kept, and the sweep is why.**

1. **The requested 12 s arm does not exist.**  `Proposed.__init__` asserts `t_rec > t_pre`, and the Stage-3 acceptance gate `T_REC > T_PRE` is part of the frozen tuple, so a 12 s arm cannot be built; the sweep's low arm is the admissible **12.5 s**.
2. **Rule R3, re-derived on the windows that actually closed, returns exactly the frozen value.**  On V2S3 at 220 m, 10 episodes closed normally, median duration **3.00 s** — the `h` floor — so `T_REC = 12 + max(3, 3) = 15.0 s`.  Stage 4's worry ("the median is far above the V1 value") came from counting the *preempted* 1.0 s window and the 9.5 s one; on the ten closed episodes the distribution is 1.0, 1.0, 2.0, 2.1, 2.9, 3.1, 3.3, 3.6, 3.8, 9.5 s, whose median is the floor.  The 9.5 s outlier is a single episode, not the typical one.
3. **The whole admissible range is inactive on this geometry.**  12.5 / 15 / 18 s produce **bit-identical** runs on both scenes (every outcome and window column equal to the last digit), because the RECOVER → NORMAL exit is governed by the geometric recovery condition (ρ ≥ 0.88, |lat| ≤ 3.0 m) once the TTC clause is satisfied by the clearance, not by a timer.  The median re-entry delay (3.0 s) equals the median window duration, i.e. the window is spent restoring the formation, not waiting.
4. **Therefore 15 s neither truncates a legitimate re-entry nor delays one** on these scenes, and it is retained.  The honest statement is that the value is *re-validated* (the rule reproduces it) and *inactive* (the range does not matter here) — not that it was tuned.

`bounded ticks` counts the control ticks at which the layered speed policy actually applied a bound.  It is non-zero only for R3, because only the rollout controller declares the manoeuvre geometry the rule needs; the supplementary `R3_no_speed_policy` row runs the same controller with the policy off, so the R2 → R3 step can be attributed to the planner and not to the speed rule.  On V2S2R2 the first three rungs are **bit-identical** (60/60 cell pairs, not merely equal to the printed precision), i.e. the handover and event layers never engage on a single threat; on V2S3 they engage but change little.  The ladder's answer is therefore unambiguous: the rollout planner is the mechanism.

## 7. Statistics

### 7.1 Why two families

The 300 runs of a method are not 300 independent observations: one seed drives the same initial flock and the same random streams on all ten scenes, so the ten runs of a seed share everything except the scene.  Treating them as independent is pseudoreplication — it inflates n from 30 to 300 and shrinks p without adding information.  The **primary** family therefore averages each endpoint equally over the scenarios *within a seed* and tests the resulting n = 30 independent units; the run-level family is reported beside it, explicitly labelled descriptive.

Family sizes: seed-clustered continuous **49** tests (7 endpoints × 7 baselines), run-level continuous **49**, binary **14** at each unit level.  Holm within each family; paired two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank (normal approximation, which is what n = 30 calls for); exact McNemar for the binary endpoints, never Wilcoxon.

Endpoints: C, min surface clearance, min TTC, ρ, max_dev/W, per-cycle time, time-to-goal (conditional on both members of a pair completing — `n` says how many did).  Clearance and TTC are undefined on the two obstacle-free scenes and are averaged over the eight that have an obstacle; a censored run never leaves the arrival / joint-completion denominators.  **No V1 family is used or mixed into these tests**: the V1 archives measure a different geometry and a different physical layer, and the only role they play in this report is as the Stage-4 inertness comparator (§4).

| endpoint | baseline | seed n01/n10 | p_Holm (seed, all-10) | run n01/n10 | p_Holm (run, 300 pairs) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| arrival | B1 | 0/0 | 1.0000 | 0/0 | 1.0000 |
| arrival | B2 | 0/0 | 1.0000 | 0/0 | 1.0000 |
| arrival | VH-Path | 0/19 | 0.0000 | 0/39 | 0.0000 |
| arrival | VH-Danger | 0/20 | 0.0000 | 0/25 | 0.0000 |
| arrival | VH-Danger-path | 0/13 | 0.0024 | 0/15 | 0.0003 |
| arrival | B-Outmost | 0/23 | 0.0000 | 0/23 | 0.0000 |
| arrival | B-PCBF | 0/30 | 0.0000 | 0/275 | 0.0000 |
| joint | B1 | 2/2 | 1.0000 | 20/15 | 1.0000 |

n01 = baseline-only successes, n10 = Ours-only successes (exact McNemar, two-sided binomial on the discordant pairs).

The **seed-level** unit is deliberately strict: "the endpoint holds on *every* one of the ten scenarios for that seed".  It is the right unit for a robustness claim (and it is where the arrival contrasts live: 19 of 30 seeds arrive everywhere under `Ours_rollout` but not under VH-Path).  For **joint completion** that criterion is near-degenerate — the 60:20 scene defeats almost every seed — so the run-level 300-pair McNemar is the informative one there; it is labelled descriptive because of the pseudoreplication.  Both are exact McNemar on discordant pairs, never Wilcoxon.

### 7.4 Where the families disagree

| endpoint | baseline | p_Holm (seed) | p_Holm (run) | Δ median (seed) | Δ median (run) | who is significant |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C | B-PCBF | 0.4659 | 0.0409 | 0.006 | 0.000 | run only |
| clr_so | VH-Danger | 1.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.132 | 1.172 | run only |
| clr_so | VH-Danger-path | 1.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.267 | 1.428 | run only |
| clr_so | VH-Path | 0.7822 | 0.0000 | 1.362 | 1.662 | run only |
| rho | B1 | 0.9141 | 0.0263 | -0.000 | 0.000 | run only |
| rho | B2 | 0.0822 | 0.0003 | -0.000 | 0.000 | run only |
| ttc_min | VH-Danger | 0.0433 | 0.2912 | -0.716 | 0.366 | seed only, **sign reversal** |
| ttc_min | VH-Danger-path | 0.0433 | 0.2912 | -0.796 | 0.346 | seed only, **sign reversal** |
| ttc_min | VH-Path | 1.0000 | 0.0050 | 0.384 | 0.472 | run only |

9 of the 49 pairs disagree at α = 0.05.  **Most of them go the way pseudoreplication predicts** — the run-level family reaches significance where the seed-clustered family does not — but not all: `ttc_min` against VH-Danger and VH-Danger-path is significant in the seed-clustered family and *not* in the run-level family, and both reverse the sign of the median difference (2 genuine sign reversals in total).  That is the useful part of the comparison: pooling 300 runs is not merely 'too liberal', it can also hide or invert a within-seed effect when the ten scenes pull in different directions.  The seed-clustered reading is the one the paper reports; the run-level table is kept only so the difference is visible.

## 8. Timeout and infeasibility census

Timed-out and failed runs are **kept in every denominator**: a run that hits the horizon is right-censored (`censored = 1`, arrival 0, goal time NaN), and a run that raises is stored as a row with NaN metrics and the error string.  Nothing is dropped.

<!-- REPRO:census -->
| method | runs | goal | time | censored | errors | infeasible events | S | P | C | clr_rs [m] | clr_rr [m] | contacts ro/rs/rr | C1lo bind | C1hi bind |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ours_rollout | 300 | 300 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 52.8 | 30.1 | 21.9 | 8.88 | -0.48 | 0.31 | 2.4/7.9/0.3 | 0.0 | 0.0 |
| B1 | 300 | 300 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 48.3 | 27.2 | 20.3 | 8.20 | -0.48 | 0.38 | 2.6/7.2/0.3 | 0.0 | 0.0 |
| B2 | 300 | 300 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 62.9 | 35.4 | 26.5 | 10.04 | -0.50 | 0.30 | 3.6/8.5/0.3 | 0.0 | 0.0 |
| VH-Path | 300 | 261 | 39 | 39 | 0 | 12.0 | 6.2 | 5.7 | 1.20 | 1.23 | 0.48 | 1.6/0.0/0.1 | 0.0 | 0.0 |
| VH-Danger | 300 | 275 | 25 | 25 | 0 | 10.5 | 5.3 | 5.0 | 1.15 | 1.41 | 1.02 | 1.5/0.0/0.0 | 0.0 | 0.0 |
| VH-Danger-path | 300 | 285 | 15 | 15 | 0 | 11.8 | 6.0 | 5.7 | 1.16 | 1.40 | 1.12 | 1.7/0.0/0.0 | 0.0 | 0.0 |
| B-Outmost | 300 | 277 | 23 | 23 | 0 | 107.9 | 75.5 | 30.4 | 15.82 | -0.62 | -0.12 | 0.0/16.8/1.0 | 0.0 | 0.0 |
| B-PCBF | 300 | 25 | 275 | 275 | 0 | 104.0 | 57.9 | 41.9 | 12.96 | -0.52 | 0.36 | 0.0/16.0/0.1 | 0.0 | 0.0 |

All counts are **per run**, averaged over the 300 runs of the method; `goal`/`time` are termination classes and every run is in exactly one of them.  `infeasible events` is the number of hard-breach interventions by the execution layer; those events split into **resolved**, **S** (solver-infeasible: no candidate in the finite admissible set was safe and the unavoidability certificate did not apply — *not* a claim of physical unavoidability) and **P** (physically unavoidable under the stated assumptions, a sufficient certificate and therefore a lower bound).  **C** is a post-hoc control failure diagnosed once per contact episode by a myopic oracle, so it is a lower bound too; it is counted on animal-animal, robot-obstacle and robot-animal contacts alike, which is why it is larger than the `C` safety endpoint (animal-obstacle only).  `clr_rs` is the worst robot-animal surface clearance: **negative for every method that actually herds** (Ours, B1, B2, B-Outmost, B-PCBF) and positive only for the VH family, which stays away from the flock and therefore does not do the task — see §5.  `C1lo bind`/`C1hi bind` are counter columns: 0 means the bound never clipped, and for C1-low that is structural (§1.3), not a pass.

The three-way split is the one Stage 1 introduced and it is what makes the census diagnostic rather than decorative: an `S` event means the execution layer had no safe admissible candidate, a `P` event means the reachable set itself was inside the forbidden disc, and a `C` event is a contact the controller could have avoided but did not.  Only `S` and `P` are counted as unpreventable, and `P` is a sufficient certificate, so the true unpreventable share is bounded below by `P` and above by `P + S`.

## 9. Timing

<!-- REPRO:timing -->
| batch (method) | cells | wall [min] | s/cell | censored | errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ours_rollout | 300 | 19.7 | 3.94 | 0 | 0 |
| B1 | 300 | 15.9 | 3.19 | 0 | 0 |
| B2 | 300 | 15.4 | 3.09 | 0 | 0 |
| VH-Path | 300 | 22.4 | 4.49 | 39 | 0 |
| VH-Danger | 300 | 18.8 | 3.75 | 25 | 0 |
| VH-Danger-path | 300 | 18.4 | 3.69 | 15 | 0 |
| B-Outmost | 300 | 15.4 | 3.08 | 23 | 0 |
| B-PCBF | 300 | 53.7 | 10.75 | 275 | 0 |

Measured total for the 2400-run matrix at `jobs = 12`: **3.00 h** (10793 s).  Per-cell wall clocks are measured under 12-way concurrency; the clean serial per-cycle cost is the `cycle [ms]` column of the timing sample (`checks/speedup.csv`).

| probe | runs | jobs | wall [s] | s/run | speed-up | efficiency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| V2S2/Ours_rollout/2000 | 8 | 1 | 155.4 | 19.43 | 1.00× | 1.00 |
| V2S2/Ours_rollout/2000 | 8 | 4 | 43.4 | 5.42 | 3.58× | 0.90 |
| V2S2/Ours_rollout/2000 | 8 | 12 | 33.1 | 4.13 | 4.70× | 0.39 |

The measured speed-up on this machine is **4.70×** at `jobs = 12` (39 % efficiency) and **3.58×** at `jobs = 4` (90 %).  Applying them to the measured 3.00 h gives a single-thread projection of **14.1 h** and a `jobs = 4` projection of **3.93 h**.  Both land within 5 % of the Stage-4 estimate (14.2 h and 3.76 h), which is the check that projection needed: its assumption — a scene-independent per-method cost ratio — is consistent with the measured per-batch costs, in which B-PCBF is 2.73× the full method's batch and every other method is between 0.78× and 1.14× of it.
The clean, **uncontended** per-cycle cost of the shipped controller is 1.68 ms at `jobs = 1`; the `cycle [ms]` column of the main table is measured under 12-way concurrency (3.83 ms) and is therefore a *comparative* figure across methods, not an absolute one.  Note that the rollout is **not** the most expensive method here: B-PCBF costs 35.7 ms/cycle — and spends most of its wall clock not finishing the task.

## 10. What survives, and what does not

### 10.1 What survives

1. **The information-set preemption claim.**  With the fixed metric, 25 of the 300 formal `Ours_rollout` runs show a genuine preemption (25 of the 30 V2S3 seeds, always by threat 2 — the designed 'threat during RECOVER' case), while `preempt_truth` fires in 0 and the frozen legacy column in 0.  The old reading was not noisy: it was **systematically** false on this configuration.  The Stage-4 D case reproduces bit-exactly under the new definition (check A3).
2. **A conditional safety advantage, stated with its condition.**  Among the three methods with ρ ≥ 0.99 *and* arrival = 1.00 (`Ours_rollout`, B1, B2) the shipped method has the lowest C (0.008) and the only positive worst-case clearance (0.64 m).  The seed-clustered family makes the C and clearance contrasts against B1 and B2 significant after Holm.  The condition is the point: the baselines with a comparable C are the ones that stop doing the task.
3. **The rollout is the mechanism.**  R0 → R1 → R2 is **bit-identical** on V2S2R2 (60/60 cell pairs) and changes C by 0.004 on V2S3; R2 → R3 changes C by -0.324 on V2S3 and by -0.014 on V2S2R2 and adds +1.51 m / +0.67 m of clearance.  The supplementary no-speed-policy probe shows the planner carries most of it (R2 0.341 → 0.029 with the policy off, → 0.017 with it on).
4. **Censoring and failure accounting.**  377 of 2400 runs hit the horizon and are right-censored (B-PCBF 275/300, VH-Path 39, VH-Danger 25, B-Outmost 23, VH-Danger-path 15, `Ours_rollout` 0); 0 runs raised.  Every one is kept in every denominator.
5. **Measured cost.**  The 2400-run matrix at `jobs = 12` took **3.00 h** (per-batch 15.4–53.7 min).  The measured speed-up is 4.70× at jobs = 12 and 3.58× at jobs = 4, so the single-thread projection is 14.1 h and the jobs = 4 projection 3.9 h — both within 5 % of the Stage-4 estimate (14.2 h and 3.76 h), which validates that projection's scene-independent-ratio assumption.
6. **The tie with B1 on completion is a real result, not a failure to detect.**  B1's joint completion (0.803) is 0.016 above the shipped method's (0.787) and the exact McNemar test does not reject equality (§7.3): the method buys a 13× contact reduction and +1.55 m of clearance without a detectable completion cost.

### 10.2 What does not survive

1. **`C1 violations = 0` as a safety statement.**  The lower bound never binds, for two independent structural reasons (§1.3), and the audit's stress configuration shows it binding 500 054 times with 0 violations only when the band is made non-degenerate by hand.  The matrix's zero is reported as **uninformative**.
2. **`preempt_ok` as a preemption statistic.**  Truth-based and, on this configuration, false in 300/300 `Ours_rollout` runs including the 25 where a preemption demonstrably happened.
3. **Run-level p-values as evidence.**  Nine pairs disagree with the seed-clustered family at α = 0.05 and two reverse the sign of the median difference (`ttc_min` vs VH-Danger and VH-Danger-path).  The run-level family is descriptive only.
4. **“Best on every column”.**  B1 and B2 have a *smaller* worst-case path deviation than the shipped method (Δ = 0.064 W on the scene-equal means, paired median +0.071 W, p_Holm = 0.0005), and the method ranks 3 of 8 on max_dev/W.  Clearance is bought with lateral room, and the paper must say so.
5. **“No collision anywhere”.**  Contact fraction is zero *for the animal–obstacle class only*; the worst robot–animal surface clearance is negative for every method that actually herds (−0.48 m for the shipped method, the same as B1/B2), and robot–robot clearance stays positive (0.31 m).  The VH family keeps positive robot–animal clearance precisely because it never closes on the flock.
6. **The Stage-4 pilot's n = 3 numbers as effect sizes.**  The formal matrix replaces them.  The pilot's qualitative headline (the event layer alone is not what carries the sequential-scene benefit) is confirmed on 30 seeds; its magnitudes are not.
7. **`T_REC = 15 s` as a tuned value.**  It is retained because the rule re-derived on the 220 m closed windows returns exactly 15.0 s **and** the whole admissible range (12.5–18 s) is inactive (§5.4) — not because 15 s was optimised.
8. **The Stage-4 runtime projection as an estimate.**  It is replaced by the measurement (3.00 h at jobs = 12); its jobs = 4 figure (3.76 h) is also superseded by the projection computed from the measured speed-ups (3.94 h).

## 11. 待确认 (explicit gaps)

| item | status |
|---|---|
| **Sensing radii** (animal 25 m, obstacle 70 m) | 待确认 — still engineering values carried from Table 13, with no ecological or hardware basis; the range *sensitivity* is a Stage-3 result, not a Stage-5 claim |
| **Graze offset 5 m on the scale scenes** | 待确认 — calibrated to this flock's p95 lateral extent (4.33 m) at 36:12 and used unchanged on V2S4S (18:6) and V2S4L (60:20); the scale-family rows are a fixed-width comparison, not a head-on one |
| **M2 stress variant** | not exercised here; every Stage-5 number is M1-only by design |
| **Fix-1 equivalence** | measured on 4 real cells (2 110 / 1 286 / 1 296 / 1 293 control ticks), not on all 2 400 runs; the argument for the rest is that the published track equals the truth obstacle by construction at zero error/delay/loss |
| **Truth-side preemption variant** | its onset shifts by ≤ 0.4 s against the publish-instant series; the shortest window observed is 1.0 s, so a marginal case could in principle flip.  It is a sensitivity variant, not the paper's statistic |
| **C1** | the formal-matrix zero-violation result is reported as uninformative.  The stress case changes two parameters by hand (`m_s_min`, `a_sheep`) and is an audit of the machinery, not a claim about the shipped configuration |
| **Baseline fidelity** | VH-\*, B-Outmost and B-PCBF are mechanism-level reproductions of the published control laws (the authors released no code); the ranking is against those mechanisms |
| **Time-to-goal tests** | conditional on both members of a pair completing; the unconditional statement about finishing the task is the arrival / joint-completion McNemar table |
| **B-PCBF** | 275 of its 300 runs do not finish; its cost is therefore partly time spent *not* solving the task, and its per-cycle cost is quoted with both denominators (controller cycle vs wall-clock run) |
| **Per-cycle cost** | absolute milliseconds are machine-specific; only the ratios between methods are portable |
| **Rollout horizon** | the planner's 12 s horizon coincides with the TTC risk horizon and was not swept in Stage 5 (the Stage-1/2 ablation covered the predictor, not this stage's comparison) |
| **`preempt_assume_ok` column** | the CSV column is evaluated against 36 animals, so on the 18:6 (V2S4S) and 60:20 (V2S4L) scenes it reads 0 by construction; the quantity that matters is `sense_animal_obs_mean == n_sheep(scene)` |

## 12. Files, commands, provenance

### 12.1 New code (this pass; no V1 file was edited)

```
v2/stage5/__init__.py       package marker + scope statement
v2/stage5/common.py         frozen Stage-5 design: methods, scenes, seeds,
                            endpoints, paths, hashing
v2/stage5/probe.py          records the controller-side TTC at the publish
                            instant (fix 1), read-only
v2/stage5/preempt.py        RECOVER windows + preempt_ctrl / preempt_truth
v2/stage5/runs.py           one Stage-5 cell (run_cell + measurement columns)
v2/stage5/matrix.py         the 2400-run matrix, checkpointed per method
v2/stage5/ablation.py       the four-rung ladder (240 runs)
v2/stage5/trec_sweep.py     T_REC re-validation at 220 m (fix 2)
v2/stage5/c1_probe.py       the C1 audit: structural proof + stress case
v2/stage5/gated_probe.py    the equivalence proof behind fix 1
v2/stage5/speedup.py        measured jobs = 1 / 4 / 12 speed-up
v2/stage5/checks.py         acceptance A / B / C / D
v2/stage5/stats.py          the two statistical families
v2/stage5/tables.py         every table in this document
v2/stage5/report.py         this document's prose template
reproduce_stage5.py         regenerates every number from the CSVs
```

### 12.2 Commands

```powershell
cd 01_Main_Experiment/code
$env:OMP_NUM_THREADS=1; $env:OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1; $env:MKL_NUM_THREADS=1

python -X utf8 -m v2.stage5.gated_probe      # fix 1 equivalence proof
python -X utf8 -m v2.stage5.matrix --jobs 12 # the 2400-run matrix
python -X utf8 -m v2.stage5.ablation --jobs 12 --probe-nopolicy
python -X utf8 -m v2.stage5.trec_sweep --jobs 8
python -X utf8 -m v2.stage5.c1_probe --jobs 6
python -X utf8 -m v2.stage5.speedup
python -X utf8 -m v2.stage5.checks --tests A B C D --jobs 4
python -X utf8 reproduce_stage5.py --write-report
```

### 12.3 Reproducibility

`reproduce_stage5.py` rebuilds every table in this document from `results_v2_stage5/` and `--check-report` fails if the document on disk is not byte-identical to the rebuilt one.  The Stage-5 CSVs carry `config_id`, `seed`, `scenario` and method on every row; the code hashes of the frozen tree are in `results_v2_stage5/matrix/_formal_batches.json` and are cross-checked against the Stage-4 snapshot by check D.
